MA-WR-F00-Q01.text: What is two plus two? Work it out, then type the answer.

MA-WR-F00-Q02.text: Count the apples on your screen. Then type how many there are.

MA-WR-F00-Q03.text: Start with four and take away one. Type the number that's left.

MA-WR-F00-Q04.text: Five plus five. Your fingers might help here. Type the answer when you have it.

MA-WR-F00-Q05.text: What do you get when you add one and two? Type your answer in the box.

MA-WR-F00-Q06.text: Six take away two. Work it out, then type what's left.

MA-WR-F00-Q07.text: How many stars can you see? Count them slowly, then type the number.

MA-WR-F00-Q08.text: Three plus four. Take your time, then type the answer.

MA-WR-S06-Q01.text: What is four minus nine? Work it out carefully, then type your answer.

MA-WR-S06-Q02.text: Start at negative six and add ten. Where do you end up? Type the answer.

MA-WR-S06-Q03.text: What is twenty-five percent of eighty? Work it out and type the number.

MA-WR-S06-Q04.text: Add nought point five and nought point two five. Type your answer as a decimal.

MA-WR-S07-Q01.text: Two x plus three equals eleven. What number must x be? Type it in.

MA-WR-S07-Q02.text: Here's an equation with an unknown, x, on your screen. Work out what x has to be to make it true, and type that number.

MA-WR-S07-Q03.text: Four to three is the same ratio as twelve to what? Type the missing number.

MA-WR-S08-Q01.text: What is two cubed? Work it out, then type the answer.

MA-WR-S08-Q02.text: What's the square root of eighty-one? Type your answer.

MA-WR-S08-Q03.text: Three squared plus four squared. Work out each part, add them, and type the total.

MA-WR-T01-Q01.text: Count the apples on your screen, slowly and carefully. Then type how many there are.

MA-WR-T01-Q02.text: How many socks can you see? Count them carefully, then type the number.

MA-WR-T01-Q03.text: Let's count the cars. Go along the row slowly, and when you're done, type the total as a number.

MA-WR-T01-Q04.text: Count every star on the screen. When you're sure of the total, type it in.

MA-WR-T01-Q05.text: Some fish are swimming across your screen. Count them, then type how many you found.

MA-WR-T01-Q06.text: Count the balloons from left to right so none get missed. Then type the number you reach.

MA-WR-T01-Q07.text: Here's a row of coins. Count them up, then type how many coins there are.

MA-WR-T01-Q08.text: Count the puzzle pieces, keeping your place as you go. Type the number when you've finished.

MA-WR-T01-Q09.text: A buzzing crowd of bees has arrived. Count every single bee, then type how many there are.

MA-WR-T01-Q10.text: Butterflies have come to visit your screen. Count them all carefully, then type how many came.

MA-WR-T02-Q01.text: What do you get when you add two and three? Work it out, then type your answer.

MA-WR-T02-Q02.text: Start with six and take away two. Type the number that's left.

MA-WR-T02-Q03.text: Four plus four. You can use your fingers or your head. Then type the answer.

MA-WR-T02-Q04.text: Nine take away five. Have a think, then type what you get.

MA-WR-T02-Q05.text: Seven plus six. Take your time, then type your answer in the box.

MA-WR-T02-Q06.text: Fifteen take away eight. What does that leave? Type your answer.

MA-WR-T02-Q07.text: Here's an addition: eight plus five. Work it out and type the total.

MA-WR-T02-Q08.text: Twelve minus seven. Work it out in whatever way suits you, then type the answer.

MA-WR-T02-Q09.text: Imagine you have seventeen stickers and a friend gives you six more. What's seventeen plus six? Type your answer.

MA-WR-T02-Q10.text: Twenty-four take away nine. Can you work it out? Type the number you get.

MA-WR-T03-Q01.text: Three plus something makes five. What's the missing number? Type it in.

MA-WR-T03-Q02.text: Something plus four makes nine. Which number is hiding in the gap? Type it.

MA-WR-T03-Q03.text: Eight take away a mystery number leaves three. What's the mystery number? Type it in.

MA-WR-T03-Q04.text: A number take away two equals six. What number did we start with? Type it in the gap.

MA-WR-T03-Q05.text: Seven plus what makes thirteen? Work out the missing number and type it.

MA-WR-T03-Q06.text: Something plus nine equals fifteen. Type the number that belongs in the gap.

MA-WR-T03-Q07.text: Fourteen take away a missing number gives eight. Can you find it? Type your answer.

MA-WR-T03-Q08.text: A number minus seven leaves five. What was the starting number? Type it in.

MA-WR-T03-Q09.text: Sixteen plus a secret number makes twenty-five. What's the secret number? Type it in the gap.

MA-WR-T03-Q10.text: Here's a trickier gap to fill. Some number take away fifteen leaves eighteen. What did you start with? Type it.

MA-WR-T04-Q01.text: Four plus three equals what? Your choices are seven, six or eight. Drag the right one into the gap.

MA-WR-T04-Q02.text: Nine take away four. Work it out, then drag the matching number into the blank.

MA-WR-T04-Q03.text: Something plus five makes eleven. Is it six, sixteen or five? Drag your choice into the gap.

MA-WR-T04-Q04.text: Eight plus eight. Work out the total, then drag the number that fits into the blank.

MA-WR-T04-Q05.text: Thirteen take away six. The numbers to choose from are seven, nineteen and six. Drag the one that fits.

MA-WR-T04-Q06.text: Fourteen plus seven. Have a think, then drag the right number into the empty space.

MA-WR-T04-Q07.text: Twenty take away thirteen. Will it be seven, thirty-three or six? Drag your answer into the blank.

MA-WR-T04-Q08.text: Nine plus nine. Work it out, then pick the number that fits and drag it into place.

MA-WR-T04-Q09.text: Twenty-eight take away fifteen. Can you choose between thirteen, forty-three and twelve? Drag the one that fits.

MA-WR-T04-Q10.text: Seventeen plus sixteen. Work through it step by step, then drag the matching number into the blank.

MA-WR-T05-Q01.text: Six, something, two, equals eight. Does plus or minus belong in the gap? Drag it in.

MA-WR-T05-Q02.text: Nine, a missing sign, then three, equals six. Which sign fits, minus or plus? Drag it into the blank.

MA-WR-T05-Q03.text: Five, a missing sign, five, equals ten. Which symbol fits, plus or minus? Drag the right one in.

MA-WR-T05-Q04.text: Seven, a gap, four, equals three. Choose minus or plus, and drag it into the gap.

MA-WR-T05-Q05.text: Twelve, a missing sign, five, equals seventeen. Is it plus or minus? Drag it into place.

MA-WR-T05-Q06.text: Look at twenty, a gap, eight, equals twelve. Which symbol makes it true, minus or plus?

MA-WR-T05-Q07.text: Six, a missing sign, six, equals twelve. Drag plus or minus into the gap to make it true.

MA-WR-T05-Q08.text: Fifteen, a gap, nine, equals six. Which sign makes it true, minus or plus? Drag it in.

MA-WR-T05-Q09.text: Twenty-four, a missing sign, seventeen, equals seven. Which fits, minus or plus? Drag your choice into the gap.

MA-WR-T05-Q10.text: Nineteen, a gap, fourteen, equals thirty-three. Choose plus or minus, and drag it in to make the sentence true.

MA-WR-T06-Q01.text: A number is written in words on your screen. Read it, then type it using digits.

MA-WR-T06-Q02.text: Look at the number word. Can you write it as a digit instead? Type it in.

MA-WR-T06-Q03.text: Here's a number spelled out in letters. Read it carefully, then type it as a numeral.

MA-WR-T06-Q04.text: Read the word on the screen. Which digit means the same thing? Type it.

MA-WR-T06-Q05.text: This number is written as a word. Turn it into digits and type it in the box.

MA-WR-T06-Q06.text: Read the number word closely. Then type the same number using digits.

MA-WR-T06-Q07.text: Look at the word on your screen. Type the number it stands for, in digits.

MA-WR-T06-Q08.text: Here's another number word. Read it, then show it with digits by typing it.

MA-WR-T06-Q09.text: This number word has two parts joined together. Read it, then type the whole number using digits.

MA-WR-T06-Q10.text: Imagine you're writing this number on a birthday card. Read the word, then type it using digits.

MA-WR-T07-Q01.text: Compare seven and four. Type the symbol for greater than, less than, or equals, whichever makes it true.

MA-WR-T07-Q02.text: Look at two and nine. Which symbol belongs between them: greater than, less than, or equals? Type it.

MA-WR-T07-Q03.text: Compare the two numbers on your screen. Type greater than, less than, or equals, using its symbol.

MA-WR-T07-Q04.text: Ten and three. Which symbol fits in the gap: greater than, less than, or equals? Type it in.

MA-WR-T07-Q05.text: Compare eighteen and twenty-one. Type the symbol that makes it true: greater than, less than, or equals.

MA-WR-T07-Q06.text: Look closely at both numbers on the screen. Is it greater than, less than, or equals? Type the symbol.

MA-WR-T07-Q07.text: Twenty-seven and seventy-two use the same digits. Compare them, then type greater than, less than, or equals.

MA-WR-T07-Q08.text: Work out both sides first: six plus three, and five plus four. Then type greater than, less than, or equals.

MA-WR-T07-Q09.text: On one side, nine plus five. On the other, twenty minus eight. Work out each, then type greater than, less than, or equals.

MA-WR-T07-Q10.text: Two sums to compare: seven times two, and six plus nine. Work them out, then type greater than, less than, or equals.

MA-WR-T08-Q01.text: You've got some number tiles and two symbols. Drag them into an order that makes a true equation.

MA-WR-T08-Q02.text: Use all the tiles on your screen to build an equation that's true. Try a few orders if you need to.

MA-WR-T08-Q03.text: Here are some tiles with numbers and signs. Arrange them so the equation balances and is true.

MA-WR-T08-Q04.text: Drag the tiles into place to make a true number sentence. Every tile gets used once.

MA-WR-T08-Q05.text: Can you build a true equation from these tiles? Move them around until the number sentence works.

MA-WR-T08-Q06.text: Look at the numbers and the symbols on the tiles. Put them in an order that makes the equation true.

MA-WR-T08-Q07.text: Build a true equation with the tiles on your screen. Check it by reading it back to yourself.

MA-WR-T08-Q08.text: Arrange the tiles to make a number sentence that's true. Use every tile.

MA-WR-T08-Q09.text: These tiles hold bigger numbers and a sign. Can you put them in an order that makes a true equation?

MA-WR-T08-Q10.text: Time to be an equation builder. Drag the tiles around until they make a number sentence that's true.

MA-WR-T09-Q01.text: One, two, three, and then what? Type the next number in the pattern.

MA-WR-T09-Q02.text: Look at this pattern: two, four, six. What number comes next? Type it in.

MA-WR-T09-Q03.text: Five, ten, fifteen. Spot the pattern and type the number that comes next.

MA-WR-T09-Q04.text: This pattern goes ten, nine, eight. What's the next number? Type it.

MA-WR-T09-Q05.text: Three, six, nine. What rule is the pattern following? Use it to type the next number.

MA-WR-T09-Q06.text: Twenty, fifteen, ten. Follow the pattern and type the number that comes after.

MA-WR-T09-Q07.text: One, three, five. What comes next in this pattern? Type your answer.

MA-WR-T09-Q08.text: Two, four, eight, sixteen. Look at how each number connects to the next, then type the next number.

MA-WR-T09-Q09.text: Here's a mystery pattern: one, one, two, three, five. Can you work out the rule and type what comes next?

MA-WR-T09-Q10.text: Follow the number trail: one hundred, ninety, eighty. Where does the trail go next? Type the number.

MA-WR-T10-Q01.text: Look at the two groups of apples being added together. Type a number sentence that shows the picture, with the answer at the end.

MA-WR-T10-Q02.text: Some balloons, and then some are taken away. Type the number sentence that matches the picture, answer included.

MA-WR-T10-Q03.text: Count the dogs in each group. Then type a number sentence that shows them being added, and finish it with the answer.

MA-WR-T10-Q04.text: Here's a group of coins with some taken away. Type the number sentence for this picture, including the answer.

MA-WR-T10-Q05.text: Two groups of puzzle pieces are being added. Count each group, then type the whole number sentence with its answer.

MA-WR-T10-Q06.text: A big group of grapes, and some are taken away. Count carefully, then type the number sentence, answer and all.

MA-WR-T10-Q07.text: Ana had nine coins, and then she found six more. Type a number sentence that shows this, ending with the answer.

MA-WR-T10-Q08.text: Ben had sixteen sweets and ate nine of them. What number sentence shows this? Type it, with the answer.

MA-WR-T10-Q09.text: A shop had twenty-eight loaves. It sold thirteen, then six more arrived. Type a number sentence that shows how many it has at the end.

MA-WR-T10-Q10.text: A jar had thirty-four sweets. Twelve were eaten, then nine more were added. Can you type a number sentence for the final amount?

MA-WR-T11-Q01.text: Tom has four apples, and his friend gives him three more. How many apples does Tom have now? Type your answer.

MA-WR-T11-Q02.text: Priya has nine stickers and gives four to a friend. How many does she have left? Type the number.

MA-WR-T11-Q03.text: A bus picks up five children, and then six more get on. How many children are on the bus now?

MA-WR-T11-Q04.text: There are fifteen sweets in a jar, and six get eaten. How many are left? Type your answer.

MA-WR-T11-Q05.text: Ben saves seven coins one week and eight the next. How many coins is that in total? Type it in.

MA-WR-T11-Q06.text: A classroom has twenty-four chairs, and seventeen are being used. How many chairs are free? Type the number.

MA-WR-T11-Q07.text: Ana reads twelve pages on Monday and nine pages on Tuesday. How many pages is that altogether?

MA-WR-T11-Q08.text: A shop has thirty-two loaves of bread, and it sells eighteen. How many loaves are left? Type your answer.

MA-WR-T11-Q09.text: A charity collects forty-six pounds in one week and twenty-seven the next. How much is that in total? Type the number.

MA-WR-T11-Q10.text: A school library has eighty-five books, and thirty-nine are checked out. How many are still on the shelf?

MA-WR-T12-Q01.text: Ana has ten coins. She spends three on a toy and two on a snack. How many coins are left? There are two steps, so type the final answer.

MA-WR-T12-Q02.text: Tom has four apples. He gets three more, then eats two. How many does he have now? Type your final answer.

MA-WR-T12-Q03.text: A shop has eight balloons. It sells three, then gets five more delivered. Work through both steps and type how many balloons it has now.

MA-WR-T12-Q04.text: Ben has twenty pence. He buys a sweet for eight pence, then finds a five pence coin. How much does he have now?

MA-WR-T12-Q05.text: A box has twelve eggs. Five are used for one cake and four for another. How many eggs are left? Type the final answer.

MA-WR-T12-Q06.text: Omar has twenty-five free minutes. He plays for ten, then does homework for eight. How many minutes are left?

MA-WR-T12-Q07.text: A jar has eighteen sweets. Six friends each take one, then three more are added. How many sweets are in the jar now?

MA-WR-T12-Q08.text: A charity collects forty-five pounds on Saturday and thirty-two on Sunday, then spends twenty on supplies. How much is left? Type your final answer.

MA-WR-T12-Q09.text: A school has a hundred and twenty pupils. Forty-five go on a trip and fifteen more stay home sick. How many are still at school?

MA-WR-T12-Q10.text: A baker has sixty muffins. She sells twenty-four in the morning and bakes ten more in the afternoon. How many does she have by evening?

MA-WR-T13-Q01.text: One ribbon is five centimetres long, and another is three centimetres. How long are they together? Type your answer with its unit.

MA-WR-T13-Q02.text: A bottle holds four litres of water, and you pour out one litre. How much is left? Remember to type the unit too.

MA-WR-T13-Q03.text: A bag of apples weighs two kilograms, and another weighs three kilograms. What do they weigh together? Include the unit.

MA-WR-T13-Q04.text: A rope is fifteen metres long, and you cut off six metres. How much rope is left? Type the number and the unit.

MA-WR-T13-Q05.text: A jug has two hundred and fifty millilitres of juice, and you add a hundred and fifty more. How much juice is there now, with its unit?

MA-WR-T13-Q06.text: One parcel weighs eight hundred grams and another weighs four hundred and fifty grams. How much do they weigh together? Type it with the unit.

MA-WR-T13-Q07.text: A pool is twenty-five metres long, and a swimmer completes four lengths. How far did they swim? Type the distance with its unit.

MA-WR-T13-Q08.text: Two planks are on your screen, each with its length in metres. How long would they be laid end to end? Type your answer with its unit.

MA-WR-T13-Q09.text: A tank holds twelve litres, and four point five litres are used. How much is left? Type your answer with the unit.

MA-WR-T13-Q10.text: You're baking, and the recipe needs five hundred grams of flour, but you only have three hundred and fifty grams. How much more do you need, with its unit?

MA-WR-T14-Q01.text: Two friends share a pizza equally. What fraction of the pizza does each friend get? Type the fraction.

MA-WR-T14-Q02.text: Four friends share a cake equally. What fraction does each friend get? Type it as a fraction.

MA-WR-T14-Q03.text: Three friends share a chocolate bar equally. What fraction of the bar does each friend get? Type your answer.

MA-WR-T14-Q04.text: A pizza is cut into four equal slices, and you eat one slice. What fraction of the pizza is left? Type it.

MA-WR-T14-Q05.text: A chocolate bar has eight equal pieces, and two get eaten. What fraction of the bar is left? Type the fraction.

MA-WR-T14-Q06.text: Two people share six sweets equally. What fraction of all the sweets does each person get? Type it.

MA-WR-T14-Q07.text: Four people share twelve grapes equally. What fraction of the grapes does each person get? Type the fraction.

MA-WR-T14-Q08.text: The question names two fractions of the same pizza. Which one is the bigger piece? Read them both, then type the bigger fraction.

MA-WR-T14-Q09.text: Six friends share three pizzas equally. What fraction of a pizza does each friend get? Type your answer as a fraction.

MA-WR-T14-Q10.text: A cake is cut into ten equal slices, and three are eaten. What fraction of the cake is left? Type it in.

MA-WR-T15-Q01.text: Tom has five apples and gets four more. How many does he have? Write down how you worked it out, then give your answer.

MA-WR-T15-Q02.text: Priya has nine stickers and gives away three. How many are left? Show your working, then write your answer.

MA-WR-T15-Q03.text: A class has twenty-four children, and nine go on a trip. How many stay behind? Show each step, then give your answer.

MA-WR-T15-Q04.text: Ben saves six coins one week and seven the next. How many is that in total? Write out your working, then your answer.

MA-WR-T15-Q05.text: A shop has fifteen loaves. It sells eight, then bakes five more. How many does it have now? Show both steps of your working.

MA-WR-T15-Q06.text: Ana had twenty pence. She spent seven pence, then found four pence. How much does she have now? Show how you worked it out.

MA-WR-T15-Q07.text: Omar has some free time, and he spends part of it playing and part reading. Use the numbers on your screen to work out how many minutes are left, and show your working.

MA-WR-T15-Q08.text: A charity had eighty pounds. It spent twenty-five on supplies, then received forty more in donations. How much does it have now? Show your working.

MA-WR-T15-Q09.text: A school had two hundred pupils. Thirty-five left and eighteen new pupils joined. How many pupils are there now? Write out each step.

MA-WR-T15-Q10.text: A baker makes forty-eight muffins. She sells three boxes of eight, then bakes fifteen more. How many does she have now? Show every step.
